### 2.3 Generic smart model-start configuration

The smart-start layer is generic, load-time only and model-neutral.

Global modes:
- Exclusive: smart config owns supported knobs; user values for those knobs are ignored.
- Enabled: default; user values win per knob, Auto resolves unspecified knobs.
- Disabled: Auto off; use user values where provided, otherwise static defaults.

Generic core owns precedence/reporting only. Adapters own typed overrides and candidate evaluation. Adding/removing knobs does not require a universal model-specific enum.

Current Qwen CUDA smart knobs:
- state_policy
- native_rows

Candidate priority:
1. preserve resident weights
2. wider qualified native cohort
3. Contiguous tie-break

Canonical QwenCuda uses Enabled.

Compatibility:
- QwenCudaWithStatePolicy supplies one user state-policy knob; other knobs may remain Auto.
- nonzero legacy profile.native_rows becomes a user override.
- legacy zero native_rows means unspecified under smart CUDA.
- explicit QwenCudaSmartOverrides.native_rows = Some(0) forces sequential while leaving other knobs smart.
- QwenCudaWithSmartConfig exposes mode + extensible overrides.

Startup logs one compact smart-config line with model/backend/mode/observation time/value/source/reason.

Physical acceptance:
- default 2B/32K/1024 Auto selected Paged64/64 and completed in ~26–28 s exact.
- active8 SDK with native width unspecified Auto selected B8 for both Contiguous and user-Paged halves.
- actual native publication {8}.

### 2.4 Authoritative live VRAM admission

Smart observation is advisory only.

Actual CUDA startup:
1. releases reclaimable cold/cache blocks;
2. queries device-wide free VRAM from the original CUDA actor/context;
3. preserves configured non-provider headroom device_cap-provider_cap;
4. clamps provider capacity to min(configured_provider, free-headroom);
5. reruns exact admission/placement if the live cap is lower;
6. then enters normal resident/model ledger admission.

A real default 2B/32K/1024 run through this authoritative clamp passed in 27.58 s exact with clean shutdown.

### 2.5 Error architecture

Typed core categories:
- Malformed: invalid/corrupt input/artifact
- Unsupported: unsupported semantic/capability
- Limit: deterministic/static/config bounds or arithmetic overflow
- Resource(ResourceLimit): actual resource exhaustion with requested/available bytes and optional scope
- State: lifecycle/internal state
- Io: underlying IO

Never parse resource prose for scheduling behavior.

Public classification:
- Resource -> 503 resource_exhausted
- Limit -> 400 limit_exceeded
- malformed/unsupported -> 400
- IO/state -> 500

HTTP 5xx is server_error, not invalid_request_error.

### Error architecture — 21 Nov 2026

The cross-layer error contract is now intentionally small and typed:

- `Malformed` = invalid/corrupt external input or artifact.
- `Unsupported` = requested capability/semantic is not implemented.
- `Limit` = deterministic configured/static bounds and arithmetic overflow. It must
  not masquerade as a measured memory/VRAM shortage when requested/available bytes are
  known.
- `Resource(ResourceLimit)` = a real resource budget cannot fit the attempted work.
  It carries resource, operation, exact requested bytes, exact available bytes and an
  optional scope. Shared physical/resource admission includes device identity, owner,
  already-reserved bytes and capacity in that scope.
- `State` = invalid lifecycle/internal state; `Io` retains the underlying I/O cause.

Do **not** parse error prose to choose scheduling behavior. Prelaunch typed
`Resource` failures become capacity/backpressure where the scheduler explicitly owns
that policy; post-submission failures remain fatal. Resource pressure in optional
optimizations may fall back only at an already-defined typed capacity seam.

`ServiceError::inference` is the single public classification boundary:
`Resource -> 503/resource_exhausted`, deterministic `Limit -> 400/limit_exceeded`,
`Malformed/Unsupported -> 400`, and `Io/State -> 500`. HTTP 5xx bodies are
`server_error`, not `invalid_request_error`. Runtime/server reverse adapters use the
shared conversion and no longer wrap `ServiceError::to_string()`, avoiding duplicated
status/code prefixes. Real host/VRAM admission paths in the resource arbiter, resident
allocator/state/checkpoint, CUDA ordinary/source-call admission, HIP source budgets,
shared BF16 Qwen/Gemma paths and backing/model sub-admission now report concrete
requested/available bytes. Static shape/file/queue bounds deliberately remain ordinary
`Limit` errors. Preserve this distinction for new models/backends.

Validation for this slice is green on the default workspace, CUDA-native GPU tests,
Qwen CUDA serving, Qwen HIP serving, Gemma4 HIP and Gemma4 Vulkan shared-BF16 surfaces,
the existing resident-ledger concurrency/pressure tests, source-call scheduler capacity
tests, focused core/engine/HTTP classification tests and strict Clippy for the changed
production crates. One combined Gemma HIP→Vulkan compile was externally SIGKILLed while
entering Vulkan dependencies; the HIP check had already passed and one cached
Vulkan-only retry passed, so no source failure follows.

Current source/tests and live TODOs outrank this handoff if main advances.

### Tracking / handoff method

The old generated handoff/SHA/archive workflow is retired.

- `CURRENT_HANDOFF.md` is the canonical cross-window pointer.
- `.agents/plans/TODO.md` is the global queue.
- Per-plan TODOs are the detailed accepted/rejected/open-work ledgers.
- Git history is the archive and provenance record.
- Do not recreate `.agents/runs`, source snapshots, monolithic receipts, per-file
  hash catalogues or durable side-worktree coordination state.
- Actual model/content identities, numerical contracts and physical acceptance
  limits still belong in source/tests/plans where semantically required.
- Historical failures stay failures. A later pass/cleanup cannot relabel them.

## Owner direction / working style

The user has repeatedly steered the project toward implementation-first,
shared-primitives-first work:

- Prefer **implementation → quick real-model feedback → controlled comparison**.
- Solve cleanly at shared layers when the semantics genuinely benefit multiple
  models/backends/tools.
- Model/source policy belongs in model/source layers. Reusable numerical, layout,
  transport, state and physical execution primitives belong in shared runtime/GPU
  layers.
- Keep independently useful model-neutral primitives even when their first Qwen
  serving consumer is rejected; remove the slow consumer, not the clean primitive.
- Exact source/reduction/state/root/resource/cancellation semantics are never
  weakened to chase benchmark numbers.
- Unsupported capability fails closed. Never silently select another arithmetic
  profile, captured case or model-specific fallback.
- Rust preference: explicit ownership, simple robust APIs, zero-cost abstractions
  where natural, targeted hot-path optimization only when repeatably material.
- Do not over-engineer tests, evidence, receipts, pinning or phase granularity.
- Reuse accepted validation for unchanged primitives.
- Validate in coherent checkpoints rather than after every helper.
- Treat fewer launches/loads/instructions as a hypothesis, not acceptance evidence.
- For small expected gains use one-binary/one-model forward/reverse or ABBA
  measurement; cross-process clock/thermal drift repeatedly produced false wins.
- Remove all temporary selectors, profiling hooks, `_tmp` runners and include
  views after the decision is recorded.
- Recent CUDA work has used ~30-minute coherent checkpoints; continue that unless
  the user changes the cadence.
- Do not ask the user to reconfirm already-authorized continuation steps.
- Never push unless explicitly asked.

## Canonical architecture / non-negotiable invariants

ZeroGravity is one Rust-owned execution fabric, not a per-model collection of
engines/servers.

- One semantic/model definition per family/source contract.
- One logical `StateRoot` publication authority.
- Canonical roots remain checkpoint/rollback/publication authority even when
  private/native/derived representations exist.
- One process-shared physical `ResourceArbiter`.
- Device workers own real asynchronous compute/events, but cannot invent logical
  commits.
- Release follows actual completion/fence/event state; completion-unknown work is
  quarantined.
- Source/weight owners survive until the real final consumer retires.
- Cancellation cannot publish partial candidate state.
- Independent sessions/roots remain independent through physical batching.
- Physical batch width is separate from each source call's authenticated numerical
  reduction contract.
- Finite captured cases are qualification evidence, never production selectors.
- Metadata/registry slugs never grant execution support.
- CPU/CUDA/HIP/Vulkan and quant/source profiles remain separate qualification
  claims.
- Performance follows semantic/source/state/ownership correctness.

The Fabric transition is complete and now forms the shared architecture:
`zerogravity-core` owns semantic/state/provider/physical contracts;
`zerogravity-artifacts` owns immutable formats/source/acquisition/store; model
crates own family semantics; CPU/GPU crates own physical providers;
`zerogravity-engine` owns model-neutral runtime/session/scheduling/residency;
`zerogravity-serving` owns reusable protocol/server behavior; `zerogravity` is the
public composition root; CLI stays presentation/arguments/signals. Do not restart
the old Fabric S/F/Q transition sequence.

### CUDA composition / serving foundation

The CUDA route is a real source-derived resident path, not a finite-case
dispatcher.

Important foundation commits:

- `4f1e827` shared source-derived CUDA composition.
- `a57590e` output-reduction repair.
- `9d73d46` compact on-device greedy/token feedback.
- `9f45471` exact decode GEMV specialization.
- `55e195c` onward: genuine ordinary inter-session cohorts.
- `b191fc6`: exact independent source reductions survive physical row widening.
- `fa703fa` / `96a7ac7`: same-frontier chunked/ragged prefill and mutual cohort
  compatibility.

Current serving uses genuine B4/B8 physical cohorts with B2 partial regrouping.
Same-frontier ragged/chunked prefill is accepted. Unequal-frontier prefill remains
fail-closed. The retained `874e67d` shared-input Ordered+LaneBlocked B8 projection
pair remains model-neutral and exact, but its ordinary-Qwen serving consumer is now
**rejected**: public Qwen3.5-2B B8 prompts47..54/16 outputs preserved all128 ID264
tokens and native width8, while selector-off/on/reverse process-order measurements
had much larger side drift than the ~1.04% favorable two-sided candidate mean.
Keep the primitive; do not select the consumer from that noisy aggregate.

## CUDA execution/performance chronology

The exact measurements/tests live in `model-execution/TODO.md`. This is the
takeover map.

### 9–10 Nov — C1 to genuine B4/B8

- Compact greedy feedback moved to a tiny device packet instead of full-vocab host
  readback.
- Exact decode GEMV specializations landed.
- B4 ordinary source cohorts shared stateless projection/head while preserving
  private state.
- B4 GDN convolution, recurrent core and full attention became genuine physical
  batching primitives.
- BF16 finite certification was folded into GEMM stores where legal.
- B4 lane-strided output head shared weights across rows without changing per-row
  arithmetic.
- Full-prompt prefill cohorts landed.
- Native width widened to B8 while stateful GDN/attention initially remained
  composed from qualified B4 groups.

### 11 Nov — dense B8, chunking and partial populations

Accepted generic K64 families:
`67586eb` ordered large-K prefill row64, `77ffc23` ordered B8 decode,
`5a75a70` RoundedSegments B8 and `2b8e90f` interleaved-pair B8.

Other work:
`74f6422` populated small contexts; `597da3f` cross-profile measurement support;
`b95acdc` B2 partial regrouping; `fa703fa` chunked/ragged state-only intermediate
prefill; `0d9a56d` / `96a7ac7` mutual cohort compatibility.

Decisions:
- B4/B8 remain native widths; B2 handles partial populations.
- Larger offered populations become multiple B8 groups, not hidden B16.
- **B16 is rejected**: 0.8B was slightly worse than two B8 groups; 2B regressed
  catastrophically. Do not resurrect without materially different architecture.
- Unequal-frontier prefill previously diverged and remains held.

### 12 Nov — exact arithmetic + reusable stateless primitives

`b191fc6` fixed the key correctness boundary: physical widening must not select a
different source reduction. Exact B2/B4/B8 row kernels, ragged cohorts, inner-major
head packing, two-segment row split, sigmoid×multiply, stateless row spans,
RMS/residual-RMS, gate, Q/K RMS and source-exact rotary primitives followed.
Several consumers were rejected because lower dispatch count did not yield
repeatable serving gain; the clean primitives remain.

### 13 Nov — stateful primitives, roots and hot-path profiling

Important decisions before the current selected B8 state path:

- B8 gated GDN primitive retained; ordinary consumer rejected.
- LaneBlocked inner-major rejected once pack cost was included.
- Multiple dominant LaneStrided<16,512> CTA/load/unpack/warp/unroll variants were
  exact but flat/unstable/slower and removed.
- A shared-memory tiled recurrent transpose was ~12–13% faster in isolated copy
  timing but slower under sustained serving; removed.
- `fe3b122` strengthened transport oracles with an independent CPU index oracle.
- `0cdfaad` retained private ragged B8 attention; current ordinary selection held.
- `d196c1b` / `bad4713` qualified private cached-GDN state binding and in-place
  alias behavior.
- `16fba0e` retained an exact-root model-neutral derived-state cache; its first
  private-GDN serving representation was ~25.6% slower despite exact-root hits,
  so that consumer is rejected.
- `2f651b7` centralized session construction and removed first-lane prefill-binding
  coupling while keeping same-frontier admission.

### Selected: `775dfa6` ragged private B8 KV

Current serving selects this.

- Extends packed-BF16 private KV from B4 to independent ragged B8 bases.
- Canonical BF16 K/V roots remain publication authority.
- Candidate fully writes prefix copy + append + future zero tail + nonfinite status.
- A single 32-root launch was rejected because it exceeded
  `MAX_BINDINGS=32`; the cap was not widened and no opaque pointer table was added.
- B8 therefore uses two reusable plane launches, key then value.
- Physical ragged bases/guards/nonfinite/multi-token/capacity1024 qualifier passes.
- Controlled candidate mean ~709.600 ms vs bracketed `60b048d` baseline
  ~722.432 ms: ~1.78% lower latency / ~1.80% higher throughput.

## Current performance frontier

Do not generalize quick non-LTO/direct API numbers to HTTP, long context, graph
capture, another GPU or another model.

- Original C1 anchor: 0.8B native ~65.22 ms vs eager vLLM ~90.64 ms; 2B native
  ~114.29 ms vs eager vLLM ~84.34 ms.
- Warm 2B B8 cached-decode traversal has historically been ~25–28 ms/token
  depending clocks/build state.
- Dense projection remains the largest measured region; the fresh family ranking
  above is the current local guide.
- B8 recurrent core, B8 KV transition and CTA256 are accepted material wins.
- `874e67d` reduces one directly timed real 2B Ordered+LaneBlocked projection pair
  from 168.230 to 155.752 µs mean (~7.42%), but has no completed loaded-model A/B;
  it is a retained primitive opportunity, not a serving performance claim.
- Recent 47..54 +16 whole-model waves commonly land ~675–705 ms depending
  clock/thermal state.
- Cross-process timing has repeatedly reversed sub-1% conclusions.
- For sub-1% candidates, direct device timing + same-process ABBA/reverse order is
  the minimum useful evidence.

## Numerical / state / ownership rules

- Exact source identity/geometry explicit.
- No backend grant from metadata, registry names or another target.
- Every numerical profile owns its arithmetic contract; no universal epsilon.
- Physical widening preserves original source reduction order.
- Canonical roots remain publication/checkpoint/rollback authority.
- Derived representations are subordinate exact-root caches only.
- Restore/reset/replacement cannot reuse stale derivatives.
- Private in-place mutation is only a physical primitive property until a
  lifecycle explicitly qualifies/selects it.
- One ResourceArbiter; no hidden second allocator/budget system.
- Completion/event/fence governs release/quarantine.
- Cancellation cannot publish candidate state.
- Sessions remain independent through cohorts.
- Canonical future KV tail stays exact zero where required.
- Passing cleanup/final cases do not relabel earlier failures.
- Compilation, synthetic fixtures and token equality alone do not establish full
  model/backend acceptance.
- Operator correctness, model distribution quality and determinism are separate
  claims. Follow `CORRECTNESS_POLICY.md`.

## l5/x2 build and GPU operational notes

Defaults:
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8`, `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`, `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` where useful,
`CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and `python3 -B` where the
host environment provides Python.

Physical GPU checks use `python3 -B scripts/native-gpu.py -- <command>` from the
established host environment. l5 is the repository/source authority; X2 is the AMD
large-VRAM execution/test host only. X2's connector shell can have a reduced PATH,
so do not treat a missing `python3`/Cargo command in the raw connector environment
as proof that the established qualification environment is absent.

Connector behavior:
- dotlink bash timeout is adjustable; there is no fixed 114-second wall.
- Long Cargo/test calls can return ambiguous null exit/success false responses.
  Never treat that as success; check processes and binary timestamp/size/executable
  bit/marker strings.
- Prefer durable `job_start` / `job_get` / `job_output` for long builds.
- Heavy debug test links have occasionally been killed without a compiler error;
  `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` is a build-only linker-pressure workaround.
- Warmed second link attempts often succeed; verify the actual executable.

> never reset/reclaim/restart/kill their workloads. L5 owns source changes.
>
> Highest-value next work should come from the live TODOs, not stale prose.
> Current likely lanes are: graph/transfer physical-identity adoption only where
> a real consumer exists, authenticated transfer rings/broader streaming tiers,
> independent larger-context numerical references when approved inputs become
> available, and measured smart-config knobs only when existing evidence supports
> a clean startup rule. Avoid speculative fixture matrices, debug-profile
> micro-tuning and duplicate paging/COW mechanisms.
>
> Preserve the project working style: implementation and quick real-model
> feedback first; reuse accepted evidence for unchanged primitives; keep
> model-neutral primitives clean/composable; favor zero-cost Rust abstractions
> where natural; optimize measured hot paths aggressively when the fast design
> stays simple; otherwise prefer the simpler maintainable design.

## Historical design foundation — retained context, not current execution instructions

The sections below preserve the original product/architecture evolution and enduring design
context from earlier handoffs. **Do not treat old “next step”, worktree, campaign or status
phrasing inside historical material as current instructions.** The current continuation is
entirely above and in the live TODOs.

## 3. Original mission and enduring product design

ZeroGravity began as a Rust-native inference compiler/runtime and evolved into a broader execution fabric.

The enduring product goal is one Rust-owned execution fabric that can support:

- text generation;
- embeddings/reranking and encoder tasks;
- image generation/editing;
- video/temporal generation;
- ASR;
- TTS and audio codecs;
- realtime/full-duplex media;
- combined multimodal programs;
- future optional training/update tasks where explicitly designed.

The user-facing aspiration is simple:

- one binary;
- one Rust SDK;
- local-first operation;
- automatic hardware selection when safe;
- explicit fit/capacity explanations;
- OpenAI-compatible serving where implemented;
- no Python inference server dependency for qualified local paths;
- the same runtime for portable and highly specialized execution rather than a separate server per model or modality.

The performance goal is measured Pareto leadership where specialization is justified, never a blanket “always fastest” claim.

The architectural idea from the beginning has been:

- model mathematics and source semantics are defined once;
- state/effects are explicit;
- portable/reference execution exists first;
- optimized hardware paths replace closed semantic regions only when legal and qualified;
- one logical session/root authority publishes committed state;
- one shared physical resource authority owns real memory/device budgets;
- device workers own actual asynchronous compute/events but cannot invent logical commits;
- serving, model loading, scheduling and resource ownership are not cloned for each specialization.

The initial vision and full early architecture remain in:

- VISION_SCOPE_AND_PRINCIPLES.md
- ../plans/ZEROGRAVITY_MASTER_PLAN_2026-10-10.md
- the current public Engineering Specification and Whitepaper under ../../docs/
- current Fabric vNext plans for the next structural transition.

## 4. Engineering philosophy and non-negotiable invariants

Priority order:

1. semantic/state correctness;
2. source and quality fidelity;
3. safety, ownership and crash behavior;
4. compatibility and user clarity;
5. stable latency/throughput;
6. peak specialized speed;
7. experimental complexity only when evidence earns it.

Rust design preference:

- clean, robust, intuitive ownership;
- shared lowest layer when it genuinely benefits multiple callers;
- zero-cost abstractions where natural;
- hot-path optimization where simple and maintainable;
- prefer a clean design over convoluted optimization when the two conflict;
- no second runtime/allocator/state publisher hidden behind “optimization.”

Hard invariants:

- exact source/model identity remains explicit;
- model metadata or a registry slug never grants execution support;
- a finite captured testcase is qualification evidence, not general runtime authority;
- prompt IDs, prompt lengths, ordinals, packet contents, capture hashes or nearest-case tables must not select ordinary production math;
- one logical StateRoot publication authority;
- one process-shared physical ResourceArbiter;
- actual completion/event/fence governs release;
- completion-unknown work is quarantined, not silently recycled;
- source readers/owners survive until actual final consumers retire;
- cancellation cannot publish partial state;
- unsupported shape/source/backend is explicit Unsupported/refusal, never silent fallback to another implementation;
- a passing cleanup or final case cannot relabel an earlier failure;
- compile/source-only success does not imply physical inference support;
- performance follows correctness;
- no universal numeric epsilon; each operator/model/profile owns its declared contract.

The shared correctness policy is:

    ../plans/numerics-and-context/CORRECTNESS_POLICY.md

It deliberately combines the useful ideas from vLLM and llama.cpp without blindly copying either:

- exact semantics/source/state checks;
- independent operator numeric checks;
- model-level output/distribution/quality checks;
- determinism/batch-invariance as separate claims.

## 5. Important rejected patterns

Do not reintroduce:

- one model-specific server per family;
- duplicate resource wallets;
- duplicate StateRoot publishers;
- generic production dispatch based on testcase/capture identity;
- arbitrary Hugging Face remote Python execution;
- metadata-only “support” claims;
- universal tolerance constants;
- hidden precision changes to hit benchmark numbers;
- KV-only prefix reuse for models with additional recurrent/SSM/GDN state;
- benchmark claims before exact source/output/ownership gates;
- a giant permanent graph interpreter in the token hot path;
- per-kernel trait/object hierarchies with no demonstrated need;
- durable agent side branches/worktrees as coordination state;
- monolithic generated handoff archives or documentation SHA catalogues.

## 9. Ordinary cached47→50 parity protocol

Current parity design was deliberately simplified.

The checked-in reference capture procedure defines how phase 1 is produced.

Evidence schema v3 contains:

- source coordinates;
- prompt;
- 47→48→49→50 observations;
- full logits;
- all state domains;
- selected IDs/max-bit receipts;
- teardown/close receipt;
- an embedded corruption digest.

Cross-process trust:

- phase 1 emits the evidence content SHA256 in stdout;
- normal wrapper execution carries that digest in memory to phase 2;
- compare-existing requires the independently supplied trusted digest;
- the embedded digest is corruption detection, not a self-authenticating implementation identity.

Removed intentionally:

- reference implementation SHA graph;
- source-code SHA catalogues;
- migration pin catalogues;
- stage-receipt authority;
- code-hash-based evidence identity.

Phase 2 does not need the historical native bundle; it needs:

- captured evidence;
- trusted phase-1 evidence digest;
- current approved model source;
- ordinary CUDA providers.

Normal phase 1 still needs the qualified native/reference bundle.

The wrapper is:

    scripts/qualify-qwen35-ordinary-cached47-50.sh

Modes:

- normal: structural checks, ephemeral legacy staging if necessary, reference capture, digest handoff, ordinary compare;
- preflight-only: structural/environment checks only, no large copy;
- compare-existing: no historical bundle required.

The source-free production router queue is not the blocker for ordinary Qwen CUDA; the model route is.

Recent fresh review found the process-signal fixture incorrectly assumed every environment could nest a bubblewrap PID1 namespace. The shared fixture now:

- always exercises ordinary SIGTERM/SIGINT process shutdown;
- preflights PID1 namespace capability;
- skips PID1 rows only for explicit namespace/permission unavailability;
- hard-fails unexpected bubblewrap/preflight errors;
- reports skip reason explicitly;
- Rust asserts ordinary rows cannot skip and PID1 rows pass when capability exists.

Current serve all-targets result after the fix:

- 89 passed;
- 0 failed;
- 4 intentionally ignored source/hardware fixtures.

## 13. Cache/acquisition current state

Canonical cache data is authoritative; human by-name naming is not.

Human projection design:

    models/
      snapshots/<digest>/...
      refs/...
      .by-name-initialized
      .by-name-state/
      by-name/

Key properties:

- runtime/model selection never reads by-name state;
- by-name projection is disposable;
- explicit aliases and automatic names live in durable human state;
- dirty modes recover projection/reverse/reconciliation;
- publication can leave a pending human update and later self-heal;
- missing state after prior initialization refuses rather than silently losing aliases;
- reset requires explicit alias discard;
- mount-boundary checks use mount identity, not just st_dev;
- process-exit/fault matrices exercise human metadata and reclamation recovery;
- canonical snapshot/ref availability is not downgraded by human metadata failure.

Acquisition/cache supports bounded, source-aware providers and offline exact-cache behavior for the implemented providers, including Hugging Face/GitHub/Xet/OCI/S3/GCS/Azure/ModelScope/object flows where the relevant feature is enabled.

No provider metadata or alias may upgrade source rights.

## 14. Device/CLI/config state

Current CLI/device work includes:

- explicit CPU/device routing;
- exact PCI/device identity;
- validated direct /dev selectors for supported DRM/NVIDIA nodes;
- NVIDIA minor is not treated as CUDA ordinal;
- aliases converge on one observed device identity;
- source/alias/device policy precedes execution side effects;
- bounded YAML pipeline/config checking;
- strict config/env/argv precedence;
- dry-run and refusal behavior.

Pipeline configuration is more complete than pipeline execution. A valid YAML graph does not imply the task pipeline is implemented.

## 15. Memory/SSD/state direction

Implemented foundations include:

- shared physical resource accounting;
- immutable source extents;
- bounded source windows;
- source descriptor retention;
- transfer staging admission;
- retained GPU readers through actual completion;
- state/root/cancellation/quarantine semantics.

Open work remains for:

- production paged complete-domain state;
- complete-domain prefix reuse/COW;
- product snapshot persistence/restore;
- real SSD model streaming;
- expert/source IO QoS;
- eviction under actual GPU completion;
- broader multi-model residency.

Do not call KV-only reuse a hybrid-state prefix hit when recurrent/GDN/SSM/other domains are missing.

## 16. Model-family status discipline

Qwen .8B/2B are the primary current ordinary CUDA correctness path.

Qwen27, Gemma4 and other families have substantial source/reference/finite backend work, but do not inherit .8B support automatically.

Keep these distinctions:

- source parser support;
- family mathematical support;
- CPU reference support;
- a finite backend qualification;
- a production route;
- long-context support;
- serving support;
- performance qualification.

They are separate claims.

Future/target families and tasks discussed in the design include broader Qwen, Gemma4, Llama/Mistral, GLM, DeepSeek, image, ASR, TTS, Whisper/Canary/Parakeet-style audio systems and multimodal pipelines. Treat these as roadmap targets unless current source/tests explicitly implement and qualify them.

## 17. Fabric vNext — historical design that led to the completed transition

Historical state when this section was written: S0 was signed in `7396984` and
S1–S3/F0–F4/Q0–Q2 were still open. The transition is now complete; use the
current resume section and closed `fabric-vnext-transition` plan for present status.

User intent:

- make the final architecture visible in code immediately;
- break pre-v1 internal/public APIs when that produces a cleaner design;
- move current working code into the new ownership model instead of carrying compatibility layers forever;
- allow private compile-safe placeholders/Unsupported where implementation is not yet migrated;
- no reachable todo panic on an advertised supported path;
- preserve all current exact source/numeric/state/resource safety;
- qualify the assembled transition once, then fix regressions in small focused commits.

Target dependency/ownership idea:

- zerogravity-core: semantic/numeric/state/provider/physical contracts;
- zerogravity-artifacts: containers/codecs/source/acquisition/store;
- model crates: family source/math/state/tokenization/specialization;
- CPU/GPU: physical providers;
- new zerogravity-engine: model/backend-neutral runtime, scheduling, sessions, residency;
- new zerogravity-serving: reusable server/protocol layer depending on engine/core, not facade/CLI;
- zerogravity facade: composition root/public SDK;
- CLI: arguments/presentation/signals only.

The facade is the composition root. Engine must not depend on Qwen/Gemma or physical CUDA/CPU implementations. Serving must not depend on facade/CLI. CLI should call the public SDK.

### Planned transition sequence

S0 — full structural skeleton first

- create engine and serving crates;
- expose top-level target ownership/contracts;
- compile;
- explicit Unsupported for pending operations;
- architecture checker updated;
- no heavyweight model qualification yet.

S1 — exact source/quant/encoding migration.

S2 — family math + GPU provider/qualification separation.

S3 — canonical state/root/resource publication and ownership.

F0 — model-neutral engine.

F1 — complete public Rust SDK.

F2 — reusable serving library.

F3 — thin CLI and deletion of shadow runtime copies.

F4 — feature parity matrix across all currently real behavior/refusals.

Q0 — one assembled broad qualification.

Q1 — focused bugfix queue at lowest shared layers.

Q2 — final full gate, physical/source qualification and capability matrix.

Only after transition:

- broader models;
- vLLM-style continuous batching/paged state;
- larger model residency;
- SSD execution;
- Gemma broad native routes;
- additional quant formats;
- sparse/MoE/MLA/Engram/MTP;
- multimodal ASR/TTS/image/video;
- NPU/remote distributed placement;
- calibrated autotuning/benchmarking.

The vNext documents no longer require or promise a monolithic archive or documentation SHA index. This handoff is the cross-window pointer. Git history is the archive.

## Shared conventions

These are byte-identical across all abird repositories. Repo-specific rules
follow the markers below.

- **Source of truth.** Live source, tests and executed results outrank dated
  prose. Start at `.agents/plans/README.md` (overview + spec), then work from
  `.agents/plans/TODO.md` (the queue).
- **XDG paths.** Where the project owns user config, data, cache or state,
  resolve it under `$XDG_*_HOME/abird/<project>` — an absolute XDG base, falling
  back to `HOME` when unset. No legacy or alternate root.
- **Shared `.gitignore`.** The block at the top of `.gitignore` is identical
  across repos; repo-specific entries follow it. Keep it mechanical.
- **Preserve other work.** Never revert or overwrite changes you did not make.
- **Owned changes only.** Commit only the paths you changed for the request.
  Before committing, inspect `git diff --cached --stat`; if it lists files you
  did not touch, stop and ask — unless the user explicitly asked you to include
  them.
- **Ownership.** A plan directory belongs to the `@owner` on the queue line, and
  the coordinator alone reconciles `.agents/plans/TODO.md`; do not edit another
  owner's plan or worktree unless the user explicitly asks.
- **Clean pushes.** Do not push from a dirty worktree unless the user explicitly
  asked to include those changes; otherwise commit/stash your own change first,
  or push from a clean temporary worktree.
- **Terse writing.** Keep code comments and docs succinct. Comments need not be
  full sentences; prefer symbols and fragments unless the user asked for an
  explanation or the topic is design-level or otherwise complex. Prefer bullets
  and engineering focus over prose in other docs.
- **Terse output.** Keep replies short and on point, preferably bulleted; avoid
  prose unless the user asked for an explanation. Be terse without dropping
  detail.
- **Git safety.** Commits are signed; never disable signing. Never push,
  force-push, tag, publish, deploy, or run destructive operations — history
  rewrite, `reset --hard`, branch deletion, or touching another agent's staged
  or uncommitted work — without explicit user confirmation for each action. A
  request to "commit" or "apply" is not authorization to push.

<!-- END common -->

<!-- BEGIN repo-specific -->

## Repository

**Topology override:** `main` is the only persistent local branch and checkout.
Do not keep side branches/checkouts as coordination state. If exceptional isolated
scratch is required for a bounded investigation, reconcile or discard it and
remove it before the checkpoint/closeout.

Start with [.agents/plans/TODO.md](.agents/plans/TODO.md), choose the relevant
plan, and read its `TODO.md` plus the specifications it links. These TODO files
replace the old handoffs, status ledgers, evidence workflow and SHA inventories.
Git history retains superseded material; current source, tests and live plans are
the only tracking authority.

Read [.agents/plans/README.md](.agents/plans/README.md) before opening a plan —
it is the rulebook for the layout. A plan is `.agents/plans/<plan>/` with an
optional `README.md` (what it is and why it exists, plus design, decisions and
references sections, opened with its `Author:`/`Co-authors:`) and a required,
extensive `TODO.md` whose completed work is grouped under the commit that landed
it and whose open work sits under `## Uncommitted`.

- **XDG project:** `abird/zerogravity`.

## Plans and parallel work

Architecture, structure and naming follow
[STRUCTURE_AND_NAMING.md](.agents/plans/pipeline-composition/STRUCTURE_AND_NAMING.md).
Model semantics belong to model crates; shared operators and physical owners
remain shared. Workload sizes and test ordinals are data, not production names.
Existing boundary debt is tracked in the owning plan; preserve numerical/source
identities and historical evidence while migrating actual consumers.

- `.agents/plans/TODO.md`: one checkbox and link per plan. Check it only when
  the whole plan is implemented and tested; partial milestones stay in its file.
- Keep transient agent scratch and execution logs outside tracked repository
  state. Durable decisions, open work and accepted results belong in the owning
  plan TODO and landing commit; Git history retains superseded checkpoints.
- The coordinator alone reconciles the shared plan: one writer, one serialized
  atomic update; parallel appends must not overwrite each other. A finished run
  file can be removed once its items are in the main plan; keep an interrupted
  run file until its work is recovered.
- Commit verified implementation, tests and plan updates together with explicit
  paths. After each commit, move completed items under that commit and carry
  unfinished items forward; do not create commits merely to record their own
  IDs. On a finished plan, check its one line in the plan index.
- When a plan grows long, move only completed sections into
  `.agents/plans/<plan>/archive/<date-or-milestone>/TODO.md` and link them from
  the live TODO.

No mandatory run receipts, source snapshots, per-file hashes, archives or
generated handoffs. Actual model/content hashes and numerical acceptance limits
remain part of the implementation wherever needed.

## Production code and qualification support

- Keep test assertions, expected outputs, fixture prompts, testcase schedules and
  reference-data catalogues in Rust test support. Unit tests use `#[cfg(test)]`
  modules; integration helpers and fixtures belong under `tests/support`.
  Standalone qualification harnesses need an explicit diagnostic target.
- Ordinary libraries, model loading, operators, scheduling and run/serve paths
  must not depend on test helpers or qualification harnesses. A feature gate
  alone does not separate them when production enables that feature. Extract
  genuine execution primitives for both callers; keep comparison, case and
  fault orchestration in qualification support.
- Model semantics validate actual source/configuration, shapes, IDs and state
  extents independently of the test matrix. Backends reject missing kernel
  implementations explicitly. Preserve real model geometry, numerical
  contracts, executable source/image/ABI identities and ownership constraints;
  these are not fixtures merely because they contain constants or dispatch.
- Do not rename a testcase whitelist as a capability descriptor, admit an
  unsupported shape through metadata, or silently select another captured
  case. Preserve a finite captured route explicitly as qualification support
  until genuine runtime support exists.
- Review callers, module exports, includes, dependency edges and enabled
  features for this separation. Enforce it through review and these conventions,
  not additional placement-policy tests. Keep meaningful numerical, runtime,
  state, cancellation and physical ownership tests for behavior changes.

## Execution cadence

- Work in substantial end-to-end units with a concrete user-visible outcome.
  Bindings, readers, helpers and individual layers are usually internal steps,
  not separate acceptance phases or coordination cycles. Isolate a component
  when a concrete failure needs diagnosis, then return to the larger unit.
- Use subagents for substantial independent implementation, investigation and
  review. A correction or validation blocker in one task must not stop unrelated
  ready work; advance other models, backends or features in parallel where safe.
- Respect the user's agent roles and model settings. Architecture/design agents
  review and propose redesigns; the requested implementation agents apply them.
  Keep those roles explicit when delegating and handing off work.
- Current delegation: GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh for coordination, architecture,
  implementation, execution and review, per the user's26Oct instruction.
  Keep file, build and device ownership explicit across independent lanes.
- Return concise final reports. Keep intermediate tool streams and diagnostics
  in run-local logs; review changed source and executed evidence separately.
- Set `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` for agent processes and use `python3 -B` for
  read-only preflight: imports must not add bytecode to sealed source packages.
- Use focused independent lanes where safe. Optimize time to the larger outcome;
  coordinate shared build/GPU capacity. Give implementers concrete invariants,
  interfaces, checks and completion criteria.
  The coordinator independently inspects code, results and failures before
  accepting or merging; an agent's report alone is not evidence of correctness.
- When fixes become circular or repeated fix/test cycles stall a task, assign
  focused root-cause work to an independent agent with explicit file ownership
  or ephemeral external scratch; keep `main` as the only persistent repository
  checkout/branch. Coordinate shared GPU, compiler and memory use so concurrent
  jobs do not invalidate results or contend needlessly.
- Parallel agents may inspect current `main` and prepare bounded external scratch
  or proposals, but only one owner writes a shared source surface at a time.
  Declare ownership/interfaces and integrate accepted bytes directly into `main`.
- Integrate completed, contained changes promptly, even within a larger unit.
  Reconcile agent results at useful checkpoints to limit drift and catch
  interface conflicts early; do not wait for every parallel task to finish.
- Commit ready changes in small logical units at useful checkpoints. Fix major
  source/refactor bugs first; track smaller qualification bugs separately.
  Reuse applicable batch evidence instead of inventing per-commit acceptance
  cycles; run the comprehensive gate on the assembled changes.
- After a commit batch, reconcile independent agent results against current
  `main`; preserve unique/unintegrated work without creating durable side
  branches or rewriting history.
- Batch related implementations and parallel contributions before validation.
  Bindings, readers, helpers and individual changes do not each require a test,
  review, physical-regression or acceptance cycle.
- During implementation, use compilation or narrow diagnostics when needed to
  resolve a concrete blocker. Avoid routine validation after every change.
- Validate the assembled batch with the required numerical/source/state,
  physical ownership/fault and serving checks. Gather failures, fix related
  failures together and rerun affected coverage; keep evidence scopes distinct.
- Run the complete `scripts/check.sh` gate last, before accepting the final
  tested batch. Avoid repeated full gates while adjacent planned implementations
  remain. Repeat broad checks only for relevant changes, failures or unresolved
  concerns; preserve all required real-source and physical validation.
- Reuse applicable accepted evidence for unchanged paths. Avoid redundant
  baseline runs and per-helper freeze, receipt or release administration.
- Keep active tool-session jobs with the initiating agent until completion.
  A session ID alone is not an ownership transfer. Verify live supervision and
  result retrieval before ending the old owner; otherwise keep its turn active.
- Inspect every case's semantic and cleanup results before reporting a batch
  pass. Successful cleanup or the last passing case cannot establish earlier
  results; preserve interrupted and failed scopes separately.
- Continue already authorized substeps without requiring another user prompt.
  Report completed end-to-end behavior, the concrete blocker and the next larger
  milestone; test counts and receipts do not substitute for working behavior or
  measured performance.

## Implementation boundaries

Preserve one Rust mathematical engine, immutable source identity, independent
StateRoot ownership, the physical ResourceArbiter, fair workers and actual
completion/quarantine. Run checks appropriate to the change and the complete
`scripts/check.sh` gate before accepting an implementation phase. Use
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 python3 scripts/native-gpu.py --require-private-network -- bash scripts/check.sh`
for actual user/network isolation with already approved inputs. On a connector
whose outer Bubblewrap shares networking, supply the private netns explicitly with
`bwrap --unshare-net --bind / / --dev-bind /dev /dev --` before `python3`; the
harness accepts that child only when it is loopback-only, differs from PID 1's
network view and inherits no sockets. Never bypass `--require-private-network`.
Allow up to eight
Cargo build jobs by default; reduce for observed memory pressure or explicit
resource-sharing constraints. Runtime/test thread limits remain separate. GPU/model
changes also require their relevant real source, state, cancellation and
physical tests; compilation or mocks do not establish inference support. Inspect
changed code and failed/interrupted tests when resuming; Git IDs are source
references.

When applying externally prepared source bytes, ensure modification times are
fresh enough that Cargo cannot reuse stale build products; unchanged bytes may
need a narrow timestamp refresh before rerunning the same affected checks.

The root README is user-authored: leave its bytes unchanged. Do not download
models/SDKs or change device privileges or recovery without applicable user
authorization. The local Renoir/gfx90c AMD launch hold remains. Use subagents
for independent implementation/review/test work; the main agent coordinates,
reconciles, decides and merges. Preserve unrelated user work.

<!-- BEGIN SNAPSHOT .agents/plans/README.md -->

# Plans

This folder is the agent planning entry point. Start here, then work from
`TODO.md`. Git is the authoritative history (author, time, diff, provenance sha);
this folder keeps the live queue and per-plan checklists.

Current source, tests, and TODO.md are authoritative. Git retains retired history; deleted takeover snapshots are not live instructions.

Cross-window continuation starts at [the canonical current handoff](../docs/CURRENT_HANDOFF.md). For a new agent that needs the complete design/decision/evidence lineage from the beginning, read the [21 Nov comprehensive takeover pack](../docs/FULL_COMPREHENSIVE_HANDOFF_2026-11-21.md). The 21 Nov pack embeds the current handoff, current owning-plan snapshots, the exact post-20-Nov signed chronology and the complete 20 Nov pack; the 20 Nov pack carries the earlier 18 Nov/15 Nov/14 Nov/October lineage. The current handoff remains an index/pointer into this maintained plan/status set, not a generated archive.

## Layout

```text
.agents/plans/
  README.md                 overview + spec
  TODO.md                   queue: Active / Icebox / Closed
  <plan>/README.md          plan details + author/co-authors
  <plan>/TODO.md            Base + Committed + Uncommitted + Tests
  <plan>/HISTORY.md         optional chronology (heavy plans)
  archive/<year>-Q<n>.md    quarterly rollup of closed plans
```

Plans are directories, flat under this folder; do not nest plans. One plan per
effort; split into sibling plans only when a design is too large for one TODO.

## Queue — `TODO.md`

One line per plan:

```markdown
## Active
- [~] P0 <plan> — @owner — <one-line> — [details](<plan>/README.md)

## Icebox
- [ ] <plan> — [details](<plan>/README.md)

## Closed
- [x] <plan> — <closing-sha> — <date>
```

- Active is sorted P0 → P2; moving a plan from Icebox to Active is the act of
  prioritising it.
- `[ ]` open · `[~]` active · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked.
- P0 requires human promotion and a named incident coordinator.

## Plan — `README.md`

Open with the plan's authorship and ownership:

```markdown
Author: <user>
Co-authors: <comma-separated AI models used>
Owner: @<user|agent>
```

Then what the plan is and why it exists, plus **Design**, **Decisions** and
**References** sections as needed. Split a section into `DESIGN.md`,
`DECISIONS.md` or `REFERENCES.md` only when it grows large, and link back.

## Plan — `TODO.md`

```markdown
# <plan>

Base: `<sha>`

## Committed
### `<sha>` — <what this set landed>
- [x] <item>

## Uncommitted
- [ ] <item>
- [ ] <item> — <blocker/reason>

## Tests and verification
- [x] <test or gate> — `<sha>`
- [ ] <test or gate>
```

- `Base:` is the commit the plan started from.
- Completed work is grouped under the commit that landed it; append new groups.
- Tests are a flat list; tick each with the sha when the commit's provenance
  group is added.
- A plan is done when `## Uncommitted` is empty and every test is `[x]`.

## History — optional `HISTORY.md`

For heavy or multi-agent plans, keep an append-only chronology:

```markdown
- 2026-10-18 09:14 — @owner — opened; claimed P2
- 2026-10-18 09:40 — abc1234 — implemented parser; tests pass
- 2026-10-18 10:02 — @reviewer — reviewed; requested X
```

Light plans can skip it; the commits are the history.

## Parallel work

`main` is the only persistent checkout and branch. On l5, do not create additional
Git worktrees for normal implementation, profiling or review: the canonical
`target/` and `tmp/` trees are very large and must not be duplicated. Parallel
agents may inspect the same checkout or use bounded ephemeral external scratch,
but durable repository checkouts/branches are not coordination state. Reconcile
finished work into main, remove temporary `_tmp` runners/isolated build output
when done, commit logical units, and keep transient logs/artifacts out of tracked
documentation unless they become stable fixtures.

## Closeout

All tests `[x]` and `## Uncommitted` empty → move the queue line to `## Closed`
with the closing sha and date. Quarterly, roll older `## Closed` entries into
`archive/<year>-Q<n>.md` and prune their plan directories; git retains them.

# Correctness policy — all models and backends

Owner: @pvl. Coordinator: ROOT / GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh.
User decision26Oct2026: use the correctness approach of both vLLM and llama.cpp
throughout all models. .8B prompts of47–50 tokens precede genuine long-context work;
CPU/CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan results remain separately source/device qualified.

This applies to every existing/future target in `zerogravity-core::targets`,
including metadata-only entries. It changes no target's execution status,
payload authorization or existing accepted numerical profile. Root README,
source/model/SDK identity and driver/recovery holds remain unchanged.

## Required independent checks

1. **Semantics and safety:** released architecture/source codec, complete
   parameters, exact shapes/indexing/masks/positions, causal state/history,
   source ownership, one ResourceArbiter/ForwardPlan/StateRoot publication,
   cancellation/completion/quarantine and final physical ownership. These are
   hard invariants; a quality score cannot waive them.
2. **Operator accuracy:** compare with an independent original/mathematical
   reference under a declared op/dtype/quant/reduction/layout profile. Existing
   source-bit contracts remain exact. For a separately declared tolerance
   profile, use per-op error measures/limits established before measurement.
   No universal epsilon or inherited permit from another backend/model.
3. **Model accuracy:** same checkpoint/quant artifact, tokenizer/template,
   inputs and context/generation settings against a pinned independent runtime.
   Compare outputs and distributions/quality under the task-specific contract.
   Different batch reductions can pass accuracy without byte equality.
4. **Determinism:** same-plan replay, batch invariance, schedule invariance and
   cross-hardware bit equality are distinct claims. Require them only where
   explicitly supported/advertised, with their own tests. They never follow
   from a seed, matching text, enum name or a passing operator fixture.

All four appear in reports, including failed/incomplete/unsupported scopes.
Interrupted originals never become passing evidence. Every physical run retains
its exact source/binary/model/driver/SDK identities and original owner's result.
No second engine or independent publisher is introduced for qualification.

## Upstream practice used

- Pinned vLLM `db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6` tests exact token/text
  equality or mutual membership in returned top-N maps at the first differing
  generated token. Its default helper does not assert numeric allclose or
  compare subsequent different histories. Default batching need not be
  invariant; opt-in invariance is a separate runtime/hardware contract.
- Pinned llama.cpp `d81235049384534c167caea52b85a694f6103d14` compares backend
  operators with CPU reference output and per-op NMSE limits. Its NMSE is
  `sum((candidate-reference)^2) / sum(candidate^2)`. Default1e-7, matmul/attention
  5e-4 and softmax1e-6 in that source are distinct operator contracts, not
  blanket model thresholds. Our undefined zero-energy/nonfinite handling is
  deliberately stricter: the pinned upstream comparison can let NaN through.
- llama.cpp model-quality work measures aligned target NLL/PPL, KL divergence,
  probability differences and top-token agreement against retained logits.
  Neither PPL nor top1 alone proves full distributions/state. PPL comparisons
  require the same tokenizer/corpus/settings; limits are task/profile specific.
- Our common helpers live at `tools/model-correctness/`. They strengthen input
  completeness/type/nonfinite checks rather than copy zipped/truncated cases.
  Measured KL/NLL/NMSE do not silently acquire acceptance thresholds.

Sources: [vLLM tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/tests/models/utils.py),
[vLLM reproducibility](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.31.0/usage/reproducibility/),
[llama.cpp operators](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/d81235049384534c167caea52b85a694f6103d14/tests/test-backend-ops.cpp),
[llama.cpp PPL/KL](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/d81235049384534c167caea52b85a694f6103d14/tools/perplexity/README.md).

## Application across the registry

| Model/task | Independent model-quality evidence |
|---|---|
| Qwen/Gemma and other language models | Pinned original HF/vLLM or same-GGUF llama.cpp; matching source/precision/context; generated IDs/text and aligned full-vocabulary/corpus metrics |
| Quantized variants | Same-pack operator checks plus separately measured source-vs-derived quality; lossless repack is distinct from lossy quantization |
| Vision/image generation | Source preprocessing/geometry and model-specific intermediate/output/quality corpus; a text-only pass cannot qualify image execution |
| ASR/TTS/audio | Exact source/frontend/alignment/state and task-specific transcript/audio quality; token metrics alone do not qualify acoustic output |
| Decision/embedding/other tasks | Released task semantics and independently declared score/vector/decision metrics; no generated-text substitute |

Unsupported/missing adapters remain unqualified. A registry slug, source metadata,
synthetic GPU test or another model's acceptance cannot fill a missing cell.
CPU/GGUF, HF/CUDA, HF/HIP and HF/Vulkan remain distinct. No quantized checkpoint
may silently substitute for the requested original BF16/F32 model.

## .8B first milestone and long context

- Preserve the historical strict single-request/batched decode FAIL101 and
  deliberate quarantine. It asks byte equality at request batch sizes1/4.
  Independently authenticated original vLLM N1/B4 already
  differ on identical frontier47 operands: the same six QKVZ BF16 differences.
  Metadata also establishes width differences at48/49; no paired original N1
  frontier50 exists in that fifteen-transition archive. Do not fabricate one.
- Default-profile acceptance compares each implementation with its appropriate
  original numerical profile and actual model outputs. Preserve complete
  same-width operator/state proofs and exact structural safety. A batch-invariant
  kernel would be a new explicitly qualified profile, not a fix to relabel the
  default original's result. The failed historical result never turns green.
- Initial prompt lengths47/48/49/50 differ from a47-token prompt followed by
  cached decode at48/49/50. Declare and test both requested paths; the current
  finite HF route's unsupported fresh48–50-token prompts are not covered by
  cached evidence.
- Genuine full-model contexts512/1024/2048/4096/8192 and then16384/32768 need
  actual independently run prefixes/continuations within admitted capacity,
  plus state/replay/chunk/fault coverage. Large RoPE positions or empty padding
  cannot qualify them. Keep current accepted ranges and missing cells explicit.
- Current HF .8B route is finite CUDA; corresponding CPU/ROCm/Vulkan full-model
  paths remain to be implemented/qualified. Existing synthetic operator,
  different GGUF and finite Qwen27B proofs are separate evidence.

Future model/backend changes use this policy and shared metrics alongside their
existing original-source and ownership checks. Complete the focused numerical,
source/state/physical/serving checks and assembled `scripts/check.sh` before
accepting an implementation; performance work follows correctness.

Author: Project owner
Co-authors: GPT-6
Owner: @pvl

# Batching, paged attention and hybrid prefix state

Design follow-up, 21 Oct 2026. Everything under implementation and acceptance
below remains pending; this document establishes no new runtime qualification.
Current source/tests outrank this inspection snapshot. Parent queues:
[serving](TODO.md), [memory](../memory-and-streaming/TODO.md).

## Existing scope and missing work

| Capability | Inspected scope | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native request batching | Original GGUF .8B/2B CUDA B2/B4/B8; B1 survivors, unequal causal positions and compatible refill | Integrate and independently qualify every additional numerical profile/backend |
| Prompt processing | Native waves consume one teacher token per request; B1 supports bounded prompt quanta | Actual multi-token temporal prefill, qualified chunk partitions and fair prefill/decode scheduling |
| KV/recurrent ownership | Private per-session state, fixed-capacity contiguous KV allocations, original admission/leases/publication | Paged state allocation, block-table attention and complete-domain prefix reuse/COW |
| GPU HTTP scope | One worker, context512, at most8 active requests; fused mode is opt-in | Separately qualify larger contexts/concurrency; CPU8K results do not qualify GPU8K |
| Concurrency | Bounded request interleaving and actual multi-row kernels | Independent-stream/event-backed overlap, with physical lifetime tests |
| Performance | Retained bounded tests/measurements, with explicit limitations | Profile-matched short/long-context and cache/batching ablations against pinned vLLM |

These are source inspection plus retained test records, not a fresh physical
run. Accepted details remain in [FUSED_GPU_BATCHING.md](FUSED_GPU_BATCHING.md).
Do not treat its historical limitations, or those in the plan README, as
overriding later named acceptance in the live TODO.

## Shared engine and numerical profiles

- Keep one mathematical ForwardPlan, model/session lifecycle, ResourceArbiter,
  worker/queue and StateRoot publisher. Add typed cache/attention lowering to
  those paths; do not introduce a separate model or serving engine.
- Preserve the accepted GGUF/reference profile and separately qualify the
  pinned vLLM CUDA profile. Storage format, quantization, numerical arithmetic
  and batching policy are independent dimensions, not two fixed engine modes.
- Bind source/loaded tensor dtypes, activation quantization, numerical/phase
  contract, position policy and state schema to compiled-plan/cache identity.
  Select the profile when creating the model/session. Reject incompatible
  cache/state reuse or an unqualified mid-generation profile switch.
- Extend the actual CLI/session/HTTP path after whole-model qualification;
  isolated operators or a diagnostic driver cannot establish serving support.
  Keep bit-exact gates where required and existing declared tolerances
  elsewhere; new paging/fusion must not silently change either contract.

## Paged state allocator — memory plan

- Add a finite page pool and per-session logical-to-physical block tables
  behind existing state bindings. Record page generation, domain/layout,
  valid extent, source/profile compatibility and reader ownership. Admit
  tables, metadata, scratch and temporary/COW pages before allocation/submit.
- Allocate KV as context grows; define page size, alignment, tail validity,
  exhaustion and accounting. Preserve the contiguous implementation as an
  independently qualified baseline/policy, not a second session lifecycle.
- Keep recurrent matrices and convolution histories as typed state domains
  with their own checkpoint/layout policy. Do not pretend a GDN state matrix
  is a token-indexed KV page or infer compatibility from equal byte sizes.
- Committed shared state is immutable. Candidate writes copy only required
  shared pages/domains, including a partially filled tail. Keep prior and
  candidate roots separate until original Ready and atomic publication.
- Pin every encoded/captured/queued/submitted reader, not just executing
  kernels. Reuse a page generation only after all real readers retire.
  Cancellation/drop must preserve in-flight ownership; unknown completion
  retains original quarantine/fence and cannot manufacture reusable capacity.
- Define pool pressure/refusal and safe eviction of unpinned cached state.
  Eviction loses only reusable cache, never a live root or referenced page.
  CPU/SSD migration, persistence and recovery retain their separate physical
  qualification gates; paging alone does not establish them.

## Paged attention kernels — serving plan

- Lower original KV append/read and QK/softmax/AV through logical block tables,
  preserving each row's causal position, masks, RoPE, head mapping, dtype and
  reduction order. Physical page adjacency must not affect outputs.
- Preserve original numerical contracts, including inactive tails and signed
  zero where specified. A different FlashAttention/fusion/reduction route
  needs its own explicit qualification; paging is not permission to change
  arithmetic silently.
- A bounded gather-to-contiguous route may establish initial correctness, but
  must account scratch/copies and cannot be advertised as an efficient native
  paged kernel. Qualify direct page-table kernels and measure the difference.
- Verify appends across page boundaries, partial/empty tails, shuffled physical
  pages, row-specific lengths and B1/B2/B4/B8 transitions. No full-prefix copy
  on every append in the intended fast path; measure actual copies/dispatches.

## Complete-domain prefix reuse and COW — memory plan

- Build lookup identity from exact source/component and effective loader/quant
  profile, tokenizer/template/processor/adapter, input tokens/content, position
  policy, numerical contract, state schema and sharing authorization. Matching
  prompt text alone is insufficient. Physical pointer/device location is not
  semantic identity; transfers require qualified conversion and real Ready.
- Implement the greatest jointly restorable committed frontier across all
  model-required domains: full/sliding KV, recurrent/conv state, indexer,
  draft/grammar/media state where applicable. Missing GDN state forces an
  earlier complete checkpoint or recomputation, not a KV-only full-hit claim.
- For original small models, compare all42 domains; original27B requires
  all112 after that model is qualified. Define checkpoint cadence and bounds,
  partial-hit/recompute cost, eviction and invalidation. Token-page boundaries
  need not coincide with recurrent checkpoints.
- Share only immutable authorized state. Fork independent StateRoots; COW all
  changed shared domains before append. Preserve private sampler/RNG/grammar
  continuation and tenant/source boundaries. Sharing a prefix must not let a
  sibling's generation, cancellation or release change another session.
- Report actual common-frontier reused tokens and restore/recompute cost.
  Keep cache-disabled, partial-hit and complete-hit paths observable; a hash
  lookup or KV-only hit is not a full hybrid hit.

## Continuous batching, temporal prefill and overlap — serving plan

**15 Nov 2026 fair-interleaving sub-slice accepted:** the first ordered step
below—fair interleaving in the existing completion path—is implemented in the
shared engine rather than in a Qwen/CUDA adapter. `WavePolicy` carries finite
round-token and prefill-age controls. Wave selection protects every eligible
decode row, retains deferred prefill owners, services the oldest aged prefill
after two deferred rounds, and rejects a configuration that cannot hold one
maximum admitted prefill wave plus all active decode rows. Existing
source/phase/frontier grouping, native band authority, Ready/publication,
cancellation and backpressure semantics are unchanged. 18 wave tests, 14 worker
tests, strict engine clippy and production CUDA composition checks pass. The
strengthened staggered-arrival HTTP proof physically passes on both approved
0.8B/2B CUDA sources with exact CPU IDs/text/usage and final 41MiB.

Every command in `scripts/check.sh` has a clean terminal pass on these exact
bytes under isolated `native-gpu`, including the full GPU feature-boundary gate,
CPU workspace/clippy, serving/lifecycle, acquisition and release/installer/Nix
blocks. Repeated attempts to run the monolithic shell wrapper as one connector

**15 Nov paged-state control foundation:** signed `0027c28` adds a
model-neutral `zerogravity-core::paged_state` primitive without selecting it in
resident execution. `PageCompatibility` requires the bound source plus
numerical/domain/layout identities; `PageGeometry` requires a positive page
extent that is an exact multiple of the caller's semantic append unit, so a KV
adapter cannot split one token row accidentally. `PagedBlockTable` is immutable:
full pages share their existing owner; a partial valid tail always COWs before
append; every fresh page is obtained before candidate-table mutation; allocation
failure therefore rolls back through the caller handle's RAII; and
`PageAppendPlan` retains source/target/write owners until the existing physical
copy/write authority accepts them. Prefix truncation shares only compatible
immutable pages and preserves a valid-tail extent. Eight focused tests cover
compatibility, geometry, full/tail pages, partial-prefix COW, exhaustion
atomicity and owner pinning; all178 core tests, strict core clippy and
`qwen35-cuda` composition pass.

**Admission decision for the next slice:** do not carry both a full prior and a
full candidate staging pair on top of a paged committed root. Ordinary admission
counts a finite inventory of complete state roots: the base path is explicitly
prior+candidate, with additional roots charged as whole state extents.
Canonical paged state + prior staging + candidate staging would therefore become
three state-sized envelopes at full context and can exceed the provider cap.
The first production route should use one full-capacity **in-place** K/V staging
pair. Gather the committed paged prefix into it, bind an explicit paged-staging
mode that permits prior/candidate identity for KV only, skip the old KV
zero/full-prefix-copy in `KvAppend`, append new rows in place, let the existing
FlashAttention read that same contiguous candidate, then scatter only newly
produced rows into private pages under the original flight before the accepted
Ready/root swap. Conv/Recurrent state stays on the existing contiguous typed
path. Qualify continued page_size-1/page_size/page_size+1 and multi-page
full-state parity before direct block-table attention or complete-domain prefix
identity/intersection. Event/lease-backed physical overlap remains later.

`HybridStateInventoryPlan` is a pure admission contract, not a pool installer.
Inputs are the actual StateRequirements, old state_bytes/root count, number of
simultaneous staging sets, explicit page_tokens, explicit max_append_tokens and
allocator alignment. It derives:
- contiguous Vector plane layout and roots*vector_bytes maximum;
- one complete K/V staging layout and staging_sets*kv_bytes maximum;
- one homogeneous page layout and the remaining page-byte budget;
- pages per committed root plus worst candidate-page growth across **every KV
  domain** for every active staging set.
It refuses if page geometry is heterogeneous, state-byte accounting differs, or
remaining page capacity cannot hold all active committed roots plus candidate
forks. Unit proof with two KV domains/page4/append4 shows4 old roots -> vector
roots + one staging set +24 pages exactly equals the old byte cap; roots2 is
refused for missing fork headroom.

Intermittent alternative runs that previously looked like cold-loader
disappearances are connector-infrastructure signals, not model failures.
Course correction after validating the **deployed dotlink v0.17.3**
`release/0.17` tree: the deployed build does not have main's newer
`SharedProcessExit::Signal` type. Its shell runner records
`JobCompletion::completed(status.code(), status.success(), ...)`; on Unix,
`ExitStatus::code()==None` means the process dotlink waited on was signalled,
but v0.17.3 discards the signal number. For sandboxed shell commands that waited
process is Bubblewrap. Dotlink timeout/cancel/spawn/stdin/spool failures use
distinct non-`Completed` statuses, and the `Completed` path disarms the
process-tree guard before recording completion. Controlled probes distinguish the
case: SIGKILL of an inner child yields shell status137, and SIGKILL of the
sandbox shell yields dotlink numeric137 because Bubblewrap survives; the
intermittent model jobs instead terminate with null exit code, meaning Bubblewrap
itself was signalled. At those failures there is no Rust panic, OOM/Xid/coredump,
surviving process or VRAM residue; `dotlink.service` cgroup counters show
`oom=0`, `oom_kill=0`, `pids.max events=0`, with no observed dotlink
restart/poll failure. The external signal source is not proven. A clean cold run
launched directly as `native-gpu -> env -> test binary`, with no inner
tmux/setsid/heartbeat supervisor, still reproduced the same null-exit shape, so
the older harness is not required. Treat null-exit runs as infrastructure-
incomplete and never as negative model evidence; do not add a warmup workaround.

the model gate. Signed `6b920a0` now owns the harness fix: existing Bubblewrap
PID/user namespaces are detected and reused rather than nesting another user
namespace. Existing private Bubblewrap networking executes directly; a
shared-network Bubblewrap gets a fail-closed socket/io_uring seccomp filter;
outside Bubblewrap the original user+network `unshare` path remains. Signed
`4688cba` additionally recognizes a caller-supplied child netns only when current
interfaces are exactly `lo`, PID1's `/proc/1/net/dev` differs and inherited socket
FDs are absent. `--isolation-info` exposes `bubblewrap-child-network-namespace`.
Direct shared-net L5 still refuses `--require-private-network`; wrapping the command
with `bwrap --unshare-net --bind / / --dev-bind /dev /dev --` supplies a proven
private loopback namespace without weakening the harness. 31/31 harness tests plus
real loopback+CUDA child-net smoke pass. The upgraded
connector reports external signal numbers directly and v0.17.4 logs every stop
it initiates. Follow-up connector forensics found exactly one stop in the
relevant window, the explicitly requested `job_cancel`; a silent `sleep300`
survived until that cancellation. Therefore earlier SIGKILL9s must not be
attributed to quiet output or a dotlink watchdog. They are surrounding
harness/orchestration artifacts outside dotlink's stop paths. Unlimited cgroup
memory, zero OOM/high/max/pids events, zero PSI and clean GPU retirement remain
supporting evidence that they were not model/resource failures. The accepted

harness plumbing; periodic output is **not** part of the model acceptance

**19 Nov fresh overlap review / first prerequisite:** a full re-read of the recent
prefix/paging/serving changes found no new ownership/scope/cancellation regression,
but confirmed that the current execution stack cannot honestly overlap resident GPU
regions yet. `PhysicalQueue::QueueState.active` is a single `Option<u64>` and the
queue intentionally dispatches at most one physical region per card. Separately,
`ResidentSubmission::complete_with_readback` observes device completion through the
trusted readback, then `finish_ready` retires the logical device event, completes the
physical resource guard and initializes writes. Dropping an armed submission marks
completion unknown and fences/quarantines. The Qwen CUDA service is also pinned to
one `OwnedCudaQueue` logical stream. Therefore simply scheduling prefill and decode
concurrently would still serialize, while detaching the current completion Future
would violate the established unknown-completion contract.

The first prerequisite is now implemented below ZeroGravity scheduling. The patched
CubeCL CUDA `OwnedCudaQueue::fork_stream` takes a same-service client clone, binds it
to a fresh `StreamId::allocate()` logical stream, and retains the same original
`CudaServer` actor/context. CubeCL maps that logical ID to its own non-blocking
`CUstream`; existing client clones keep their prior stream. Cross-stream dependencies
remain explicitly unsafe/caller-owned. `OwnedCudaEvent` is non-clone and owns one
CUDA event on one exact actor/logical stream, with record/query/wait/destroy; it proves
physical stream completion only and grants no buffer lease, initialization or
StateRoot publication authority.

Physical L5 qualification uses two completely disjoint8MiB buffers. It enqueues one

disjoint_buffers=true events_recorded_before_wait=true primary_ready_before_wait=true
secondary_ready_before_wait=false readback=exact`.

This **does not** close physical prefill/decode overlap.

**19 Nov resident event/lease lifetime follow-up:** `ResidentCudaInFlight<'a>` now
wraps the exact original armed `ResidentSubmission<'a>` plus one same-service
`OwnedCudaEvent`. It deliberately does not own/release the `ActiveSlot`; queue width and
worker behavior stay unchanged. `into_cuda_in_flight(&OwnedCudaQueue)` is unsafe and
records the event itself on that queue; the caller must prove this is the exact stream
that received all commands covered by the submission and that no later command is
enqueued. Same-service identity alone is not accepted as cross-stream ordering proof. Event readiness is only a physical completion witness.
For normal completion, the object waits/queries the CUDA event and then consumes the
unchanged `ResidentSubmission::complete_with_readback`, so numerical/status validation
still precedes `finish_ready`, logical event retirement, physical-work completion and

`CancellationRequested`, the CUDA event is waited, then `report_physical_ready` retires
the cancelled event and the physical guard completes; no submitted Write is marked
initialized and no `ResidentReady` is created. If the object is dropped unresolved,
its armed submission is dropped first, preserving the current completion-unknown
ledger state, service/card fence, exact lease quarantine and completion-owner retention;
only afterward is the CUDA event token destroyed.
